subject: Azure private offer — commission tranching & tax treatment for channel partners
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@cloudscale.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private offer — channel commission structure + tax questions

Irene,

Thanks for taking our RFP—attached is the CloudScale RFP Q4 (attached). A couple of items came up internally that I wanted to confirm before the procurement kickoff next week:

- We need the private offer to show a channel commission split that can be tranch-based (i.e., higher commission on first 12 months, lower on true-up). Can Redwood support a two-tranche commission waterfall on private offers?
- How do you handle VAT/sales tax and US withholding treatment on partner pass-through payments? We sell via a US reseller and need to confirm invoicing flow—CloudScale will be billed by the reseller, but we want to ensure tax withholding doesn't get eaten by commissions.
- Is there any restriction on listing price vs. private offer price for the marketplace SKU? Procurement asked if list price must stay within 10% of the private offer list.

Attached: CloudScale_RFP_Q4.pdf (RFP summary)

Can you loop in whoever handles channel compensation? Would like an answer tomorrow if possible.

Thanks,
Mike Turner
VP, Procurement
CloudScale
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — channel commission structure + tax questions

Mike — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (Channel Sales) and Naomi (Revenue Ops) to confirm details. High level answers below, we'll follow up with a short proposal and a term sheet: 

- Commission tranching: Yes — we can implement a two-stage commission waterfall on private offers (Upfront % on committed ARR/first 12 months + True-up % on overage/renewal). Need to capture how CloudScale wants the trigger windows and payout cadence.
- Tax handling: Redwood invoices are normally issued to the buyer (reseller or end-customer) per marketplace flow. For US withholding and VAT, we typically include an appendix in the reseller agreement that clarifies net-of-tax treatment and indicates whether commissions are grossed up. Naomi — can you confirm Redwood's standard stance on withholding and whether we can gross-up for this deal?
- List price vs private offer price: We can set a private offer price that differs from the public list, but marketplace rules vary by cloud. Azure allows private offers with different list/offer relationships — we usually keep the difference within a reasonable band to avoid marketplace scrutiny. I will flag this with Marketplaces ops if CloudScale needs a bigger delta.

I'll prepare a 1-page term sheet (will attach AZ_Private_Offer_Term_Sheet.xlsx) with commission tranches and proposed payout schedule. Ben — can you propose the tranche splits you want to show to CloudScale?

Irene
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — channel commission structure + tax questions

Irene/Naomi — suggested commission tranching we typically propose for a deal of this size (CloudScale is targeted commit $1.2M year one):

- Tranche A (commit execution window, months 1–12): 6.0% of net revenue (paid monthly as invoices collect).
- Tranche B (true-up/overage and renewal months 13–24): 2.5% of net revenue (paid on quarterly true-up).
- Accrual vs payout: We accrue at invoicing and payout after settlement to reduce clawback risk.
- Residuals: No residual commission beyond tranche B for marketplace transacted revenue unless CloudScale requests a multi-year reseller incentive.

Tax/withholding notes:
- If the reseller is billing CloudScale and remitting payments to Redwood, Redwood will issue invoices to the reseller. Withholding by the reseller reduces the net amount to Redwood unless we agree to a gross-up. Gross-up is possible but requires a revenue ops signoff and will reduce the net effective margin for the reseller (we price accordingly).
- For US sales tax: typically handled by the reseller's tax profile; Redwood will supply tax invoices on request for audit.

I attached a draft term sheet (AZ_Private_Offer_Term_Sheet.xlsx) with the proposed splits and sample payout schedule. Naomi — can you confirm if we can accommodate a gross-up clause and whether finance needs an alternate invoicing flow?

Ben Carter
Senior Channel Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: AZ_Private_Offer_Term_Sheet.xlsx (term sheet draft, commission waterfall tab)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@cloudscale.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — commission tranching & tax questions

Mike / CloudScale team — quick finance confirmation and next steps: 

1) Gross-up: We can include a gross-up clause to protect Redwood/net commission if the reseller withholds taxes, but this will be reflected in the private offer economics (we typically factor gross-up into the net revenue definition). If CloudScale wants the reseller to pick up withholding, we'd need a signed addendum from the reseller acknowledging tax responsibility.

2) Invoicing flow: Marketplaces (Azure) invoice flows vary. For private offers where reseller is the transacting party, Redwood invoices the reseller. We can add a note in the term sheet that Redwood will supply supporting tax docs (VAT invoices, W-8/W-9 as applicable) within 10 business days of request.

3) List vs private price: Azure does allow private offers with list price variance. If CloudScale requires a >15% delta from public list, we should flag the marketplace ops team for review — it can trigger listing validation and potentially delay private offer acceptance.

Action items: 
- Ben to confirm final tranche percentages in the attached term sheet (done).
- Irene to approve term sheet language on gross-up and invoicing flow.
- Mike to confirm whether CloudScale prefers the reseller to accept withholding or wants Redwood to gross-up.

I'll also surface a short reseller tax appendix that we can attach to the offer. Marcus — please add the reseller appendix draft to the HubSpot deal and link the DocuSign envelope once legal signs off.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
